findings.title: Exclusion constraint over an EQL term is silently rebuilt as a plain index
findings.label: valid
findings.note: The backing index of an exclusion constraint has relkind 'i' with no pg_inherits row, so it is classified 'index'; the constraint is only reached through an internal dependency that points the other way; pg_get_indexdef replay creates a plain index, and verification never checks indisexclusion or constraints.

findings.title: Customer tables locked for the whole index rebuild during upgrade
findings.label: valid
findings.note: The bundle's DROP SCHEMA CASCADE, the non-concurrent CREATE INDEX replay and ANALYZE all run in one transaction (lines 678-691), so table locks taken at the drop are held for the whole rebuild, and the README only says to use a maintenance window.

findings.title: Upgrades that previously succeeded now exit 1 for databases with views, policies or partitioned indexes on EQL
findings.label: valid
findings.note: Partitioned and attached indexes plus all non-index dependants are classified unsafe and refused, and upgrade.ts maps the refusal to exit 1, a real contract change with no CLI path for partitioned tables.

findings.title: Rebuilt index silently moves to the default tablespace
findings.label: valid
findings.note: pg_get_indexdef(oid) omits the TABLESPACE clause, and neither the capture query nor VERIFY_REBUILT_INDEXES_SQL reads reltablespace, so rebuilt indexes silently land in default_tablespace.
